payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a major aging pathway in sodium-flow systems. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold, retracting the earlier unnormalized claim. The cell has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg and a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its key limitation is a hard operating-temperature floor of 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
